import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Covering problem of Rado

Let $S$ be a finite family of squares in the plane with sides parallel to the coordinate axes
and whose union has area $1$. A subfamily $I$ of $S$ is *independent* if its squares are pairwise
disjoint, which we read as having pairwise disjoint interiors (squares may share boundary points;
this reading does not change the constant below). Tibor Radó (1928) asked how small the largest
area covered by an independent subfamily of $S$ can be, i.e. for the value of
$$F(\text{square}) = \inf_S \sup_I |I|,$$
where $S$ ranges over such families, $I$ over the independent subfamilies of $S$ and $|I|$ is the
area covered by $I$.

Radó proved $F(\text{square}) \geq 1/9$ and conjectured $F(\text{square}) = 1/4$. The conjecture
holds for families of congruent squares (Sokolin, R. Rado, Zalgaller), but Ajtai (1973) disproved
it in general with a family for which every independent subfamily covers at most $1/4 - 1/1728$ of
the total area. The best known bounds are $1/8.4797 \leq F(\text{square}) \leq 1/4 - 1/384$
(Bereg, Dumitrescu, Jiang). The exact value of $F(\text{square})$ is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Covering problem of Rado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/covering_problem_of_Rado)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ra28] Radó, T., _Sur un problème relatif à un théorème de Vitali_,
  Fundamenta Mathematicae 11 (1928), 228–229.
- [Aj73] Ajtai, M., _The solution of a problem of T. Radó_,
  Bull. Acad. Polon. Sci. Sér. Sci. Math. Astronom. Phys. 21 (1973), 61–63.
- [BDJ10] Bereg, S., Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., _On covering problems of Rado_,
  Algorithmica 57 (2010), 538–561.
  [doi:10.1007/s00453-009-9298-z](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00453-009-9298-z)
-/

blocks.code:
def axisParallelSquare (a : ℝ²) (s : ℝ) : Set ℝ² :=
  {p | ∀ i, p i ∈ Set.Icc (a i) (a i + s)}
blocks.docstring:
The closed axis-parallel square $[a_0, a_0 + s] \times [a_1, a_1 + s]$ with lower-left corner `a`
and side length `s`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Set.Icc` on `ℝ²` (no order instance on `EuclideanSpace`/`PiLp`), `parallelepiped` (MovingSofa.unitSquare; not translatable/scalable conveniently), `SquarePacking.Square` (open, anchored at the origin, local to that file).
justification.name: CoveringProblemOfRado.axisParallelSquare
justification.why_needed: Concrete closed axis-parallel square [a₀,a₀+s]×[a₁,a₁+s] in ℝ²; needed to say what 'axis-parallel square' means. Kept in the problem file since it is problem-specific.

blocks.name: axisParallelSquare

blocks.code:
def IsAxisParallelSquare (Q : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a : ℝ²) (s : ℝ), 0 < s ∧ Q = axisParallelSquare a s
blocks.docstring:
A set `Q` is an *axis-parallel square* if it is a closed square with sides parallel to the
coordinate axes and positive side length.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib/FormalConjecturesForMathlib; `InscribedSquare.IsRectangle` is about four vertices, not sets.
justification.name: CoveringProblemOfRado.IsAxisParallelSquare
justification.why_needed: Predicate 'Q is an axis-parallel square of positive side length' so families can be `Finset (Set ℝ²)`.

blocks.name: IsAxisParallelSquare
blocks.text:
/-- A set `Q` is an *axis-parallel square* if it is a closed square with sides parallel to the
coordinate axes and positive side length. -/
def IsAxisParallelSquare (Q : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a : ℝ²) (s : ℝ), 0 < s ∧ Q = axisParallelSquare a s

blocks.code:
def IsSquareFamily (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : Prop :=
  ∀ Q ∈ S, IsAxisParallelSquare Q
blocks.docstring:
A finite family of sets is a *square family* if each of its members is an axis-parallel
square.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Inline `∀ Q ∈ S, …`; a named predicate keeps the statements readable.
justification.name: CoveringProblemOfRado.IsSquareFamily
justification.why_needed: 'Finitely many axis-parallel squares': every member of a Finset of sets is an axis-parallel square.

blocks.name: IsSquareFamily
blocks.text:
/-- A finite family of sets is a *square family* if each of its members is an axis-parallel
square. -/
def IsSquareFamily (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : Prop :=
  ∀ Q ∈ S, IsAxisParallelSquare Q

blocks.code:
def IsIndependent (I : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : Prop :=
  (I : Set (Set ℝ²)).PairwiseDisjoint interior
blocks.docstring:
A finite family of sets is *independent* if its members have pairwise disjoint interiors.
For squares this means that no two of them overlap, though they may share boundary points.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Set.PairwiseDisjoint` (used directly, applied to `interior`); `Pairwise Disjoint` on closed sets would forbid touching squares.
justification.name: CoveringProblemOfRado.IsIndependent

blocks.name: IsIndependent
blocks.text:
/-- A finite family of sets is *independent* if its members have pairwise disjoint interiors.
For squares this means that no two of them overlap, though they may share boundary points. -/
def IsIndependent (I : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : Prop :=
  (I : Set (Set ℝ²)).PairwiseDisjoint interior

blocks.code:
noncomputable def maxIndependentArea (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (I : Finset (Set ℝ²)) (_ : I ⊆ S) (_ : IsIndependent I), volume (⋃ Q ∈ I, Q)
blocks.docstring:
The largest area covered by an independent subfamily of the finite family `S`.
Since `S` has finitely many subfamilies, this supremum is a maximum.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Finset.sup` over the powerset (needs decidability); `⨆` over subfamilies is cleaner.
justification.name: CoveringProblemOfRado.maxIndependentArea
justification.why_needed: The largest area covered by an independent subfamily of S, the inner sup of Radó's F.

blocks.name: maxIndependentArea
blocks.text:
/-- The largest area covered by an independent subfamily of the finite family `S`.
Since `S` has finitely many subfamilies, this supremum is a maximum. -/
noncomputable def maxIndependentArea (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (I : Finset (Set ℝ²)) (_ : I ⊆ S) (_ : IsIndependent I), volume (⋃ Q ∈ I, Q)

blocks.docstring:
The set of values of `maxIndependentArea S`, where `S` ranges over the finite families of
axis-parallel squares whose union has area $1$. Its infimum is Radó's constant $F(\text{square})$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Inlining the set-builder as in MoserWorm.lean; a named set avoids repeating it in six statements.
justification.name: CoveringProblemOfRado.radoValues
justification.why_needed: The set of values whose infimum is F(square), so the slot reads `IsGLB radoValues answer(sorry)` and the bounds can be stated uniformly.

blocks.name: radoValues
blocks.text:
/--
The set of values of `maxIndependentArea S`, where `S` ranges over the finite families of
axis-parallel squares whose union has area $1$. Its infimum is Radó's constant $F(\text{square})$.
-/
def radoValues : Set ℝ≥0∞ :=
  {maxIndependentArea S | (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) (_ : IsSquareFamily S)
    (_ : volume (⋃ Q ∈ S, Q) = 1)}

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem volume_axisParallelSquare (a : ℝ²) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    volume (axisParallelSquare a s) = ENNReal.ofReal (s ^ 2) := by
  have h : axisParallelSquare a s =
      WithLp.ofLp ⁻¹' Set.Icc (WithLp.ofLp a) (WithLp.ofLp a + fun _ => s) := by
    ext p
    simp [axisParallelSquare, Set.mem_Icc, Pi.le_def, forall_and]
  rw [h, (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin 2)).measure_preimage
    measurableSet_Icc.nullMeasurableSet, Real.volume_Icc_pi]
  simp [sq, ENNReal.ofReal_mul hs]
blocks.docstring: An axis-parallel square of side length `s` has area $s^2$.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem maxIndependentArea_singleton (Q : Set ℝ²) : maxIndependentArea {Q} = volume Q := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · refine iSup₂_le fun I hI => iSup_le fun _ => measure_mono ?_
    exact Set.iUnion₂_subset fun Q' hQ' => by
      rw [Finset.mem_singleton.mp (hI hQ')]
  · have h1 : IsIndependent {Q} := by simp [IsIndependent]
    have h2 : ({Q} : Finset (Set ℝ²)) ⊆ {Q} := Finset.Subset.refl _
    calc volume Q = volume (⋃ Q' ∈ ({Q} : Finset (Set ℝ²)), Q') := by simp
      _ ≤ _ := le_iSup₂_of_le (f := fun I (_ : I ⊆ {Q}) =>
          ⨆ (_ : IsIndependent I), volume (⋃ Q' ∈ I, Q')) {Q} h2 (le_iSup_of_le h1 le_rfl)
blocks.docstring: The largest area covered by an independent subfamily of a single set is its area.
blocks.name: maxIndependentArea_singleton

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem maxIndependentArea_singleton (Q : Set ℝ²) : maxIndependentArea {Q} = volume Q := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · refine iSup₂_le fun I hI => iSup_le fun _ => measure_mono ?_
    exact Set.iUnion₂_subset fun Q' hQ' => by
      rw [Finset.mem_singleton.mp (hI hQ')]
  · have h1 : IsIndependent {Q} := by simp [IsIndependent]
    have h2 : ({Q} : Finset (Set ℝ²)) ⊆ {Q} := Finset.Subset.refl _
    calc volume Q = volume (⋃ Q' ∈ ({Q} : Finset (Set ℝ²)), Q') := by simp
      _ ≤ _ := le_iSup₂_of_le (f := fun I (_ : I ⊆ {Q}) =>
          ⨆ (_ : IsIndependent I), volume (⋃ Q' ∈ I, Q')) {Q} h2 (le_iSup_of_le h1 le_rfl)

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem one_mem_radoValues : 1 ∈ radoValues := by
  refine ⟨{axisParallelSquare 0 1}, fun Q hQ => ⟨0, 1, one_pos, Finset.mem_singleton.mp hQ⟩,
    ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [volume_axisParallelSquare]
  · simp [maxIndependentArea_singleton, volume_axisParallelSquare]
blocks.docstring:
The family consisting of the unit square alone has value $1$. In particular `radoValues` is
nonempty, so it has a unique greatest lower bound.

@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado : IsGLB radoValues answer(sorry) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**The covering problem of Rado.**
If the union of finitely many axis-parallel squares has unit area, how small can the largest
area covered by a subfamily of pairwise disjoint squares be? That is, what is the greatest lower
bound $F(\text{square})$ of the largest area covered by an independent subfamily, taken over all
finite families of axis-parallel squares whose union has area $1$?

Here "disjoint" is read as having disjoint interiors, so squares of the subfamily may touch
along their boundaries. This does not change the value of $F(\text{square})$.

claims.decomposer_note: Asks for Radó's constant F(square) = inf over finite (nonempty) families S of axis-parallel squares of arbitrary positive side lengths, normalised so the union has area 1, of the maximum total area of a pairwise-disjoint subfamily (read 'disjoint' as non-overlapping interiors, since boundary overlaps have measure zero); the only candidate answer asserted in the sources is Radó's conjecture that the constant equals 1/4 (guaranteed area ≥ 1/4, and sharp), which Ajtai refuted (F ≤ 1/4 − 1/1728), so the Prop is that refuted candidate (research solved, stated negated) while the exact value stays open with known bounds 1/8.4797 ≤ F ≤ 1/4 − 1/384 and would otherwise take an `answer(sorry)` for the infimum as in MoserWorm.lean.
claims.reviewer_why: The verbatim statement is a question ('how small can … be?') and the header status is 'open', so the faithful slot statement is the repository's answer(sorry) idiom for an optimisation constant, `IsGLB radoValues answer(sorry)` (research open), exactly as MoserWorm.lean does. c07's definitions match the intended F(square): S ranges over finite families (Finset) of closed axis-parallel squares with arbitrary positive side lengths, hypothesis volume(⋃S)=1 (excludes the empty family), `maxIndependentArea S` is a finite ⨆ (hence a maximum, includes the empty subfamily → 0) over subfamilies whose interiors are pairwise disjoint (I checked in Lean that `interior (axisParallelSquare a s)` is the open square, so this is the 'non-overlapping interiors' reading demanded by the notes; it also gives the same infimum as strict disjointness by an enlargement argument), and radoValues is nonempty (proved test `one_mem_radoValues`) so the GLB is unique and answer(sorry) is genuinely constrained. c07 also has proved API/test lemmas. The refuted candidate from the notes is shipped as the separate `research solved` variant `¬ IsGLB radoValues (1/4)` rather than as the slot, since the slot text/status are the open question. My edits to c07: variants renamed to `covering_problem_of_rado.variants.*`, API tags, and the slot docstring spells out the disjointness convention. c01/c03/c05/c08 are equivalent faithful formulations (c01 lacks tests and uses `Fin 2 → ℝ`; c03 uses ℝ via volume.real; c08 uses `radoConstant = answer(sorry)`); c02/c04/c06 instead state only the negated refuted 1/4 candidate as the slot (research solved), which is a true theorem but not the open question asked by the statement and conflicts with Status: open.

decomposition_objections.text: The notes say the slot's Prop should be Radó's refuted candidate (F = 1/4, negated, research solved) while the task header fixes the status as 'open' and requires the slot's category tag to match. The verbatim statement is a question ('how small can … be?'), so I formalized the slot itself as the open question `IsGLB radoValues answer(sorry)` (research open), as the notes' own fallback ('would otherwise take an answer(sorry) for the infimum as in MoserWorm.lean') and the repository's answer() convention prescribe. The refuted candidate is included as the separate declaration `rado_conjecture : ¬ IsGLB radoValues (1/4)` (research solved), together with the known bounds, so nothing from the notes is lost.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Covering problem of Rado

Let $S$ be a finite family of squares in the plane with sides parallel to the coordinate axes
and whose union has area $1$. A subfamily $I$ of $S$ is *independent* if its squares are pairwise
disjoint, which we read as having pairwise disjoint interiors (squares may share boundary points;
this reading does not change the constant below). Tibor Radó (1928) asked how small the largest
area covered by an independent subfamily of $S$ can be, i.e. for the value of
$$F(\text{square}) = \inf_S \sup_I |I|,$$
where $S$ ranges over such families, $I$ over the independent subfamilies of $S$ and $|I|$ is the
area covered by $I$.

Radó proved $F(\text{square}) \geq 1/9$ and conjectured $F(\text{square}) = 1/4$. The conjecture
holds for families of congruent squares (Sokolin, R. Rado, Zalgaller), but Ajtai (1973) disproved
it in general with a family for which every independent subfamily covers at most $1/4 - 1/1728$ of
the total area. The best known bounds are $1/8.4797 \leq F(\text{square}) \leq 1/4 - 1/384$
(Bereg, Dumitrescu, Jiang). The exact value of $F(\text{square})$ is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Covering problem of Rado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/covering_problem_of_Rado)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ra28] Radó, T., _Sur un problème relatif à un théorème de Vitali_,
  Fundamenta Mathematicae 11 (1928), 228–229.
- [Aj73] Ajtai, M., _The solution of a problem of T. Radó_,
  Bull. Acad. Polon. Sci. Sér. Sci. Math. Astronom. Phys. 21 (1973), 61–63.
- [BDJ10] Bereg, S., Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., _On covering problems of Rado_,
  Algorithmica 57 (2010), 538–561.
  [doi:10.1007/s00453-009-9298-z](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00453-009-9298-z)
-/

open MeasureTheory
open scoped EuclideanGeometry ENNReal

namespace CoveringProblemOfRado

/--
The closed axis-parallel square $[a_0, a_0 + s] \times [a_1, a_1 + s]$ with lower-left corner `a`
and side length `s`.
-/
def axisParallelSquare (a : ℝ²) (s : ℝ) : Set ℝ² :=
  {p | ∀ i, p i ∈ Set.Icc (a i) (a i + s)}

/-- A set `Q` is an *axis-parallel square* if it is a closed square with sides parallel to the
coordinate axes and positive side length. -/
def IsAxisParallelSquare (Q : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a : ℝ²) (s : ℝ), 0 < s ∧ Q = axisParallelSquare a s

/-- A finite family of sets is a *square family* if each of its members is an axis-parallel
square. -/
def IsSquareFamily (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : Prop :=
  ∀ Q ∈ S, IsAxisParallelSquare Q

/-- A finite family of sets is *independent* if its members have pairwise disjoint interiors.
For squares this means that no two of them overlap, though they may share boundary points. -/
def IsIndependent (I : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : Prop :=
  (I : Set (Set ℝ²)).PairwiseDisjoint interior

/-- The largest area covered by an independent subfamily of the finite family `S`.
Since `S` has finitely many subfamilies, this supremum is a maximum. -/
noncomputable def maxIndependentArea (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (I : Finset (Set ℝ²)) (_ : I ⊆ S) (_ : IsIndependent I), volume (⋃ Q ∈ I, Q)

/--
The set of values of `maxIndependentArea S`, where `S` ranges over the finite families of
axis-parallel squares whose union has area $1$. Its infimum is Radó's constant $F(\text{square})$.
-/
def radoValues : Set ℝ≥0∞ :=
  {maxIndependentArea S | (S : Finset (Set ℝ²)) (_ : IsSquareFamily S)
    (_ : volume (⋃ Q ∈ S, Q) = 1)}

/-- An axis-parallel square of side length `s` has area $s^2$. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem volume_axisParallelSquare (a : ℝ²) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    volume (axisParallelSquare a s) = ENNReal.ofReal (s ^ 2) := by
  have h : axisParallelSquare a s =
      WithLp.ofLp ⁻¹' Set.Icc (WithLp.ofLp a) (WithLp.ofLp a + fun _ => s) := by
    ext p
    simp [axisParallelSquare, Set.mem_Icc, Pi.le_def, forall_and]
  rw [h, (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp (Fin 2)).measure_preimage
    measurableSet_Icc.nullMeasurableSet, Real.volume_Icc_pi]
  simp [sq, ENNReal.ofReal_mul hs]

/-- The largest area covered by an independent subfamily of a single set is its area. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem maxIndependentArea_singleton (Q : Set ℝ²) : maxIndependentArea {Q} = volume Q := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · refine iSup₂_le fun I hI => iSup_le fun _ => measure_mono ?_
    exact Set.iUnion₂_subset fun Q' hQ' => by
      rw [Finset.mem_singleton.mp (hI hQ')]
  · have h1 : IsIndependent {Q} := by simp [IsIndependent]
    have h2 : ({Q} : Finset (Set ℝ²)) ⊆ {Q} := Finset.Subset.refl _
    calc volume Q = volume (⋃ Q' ∈ ({Q} : Finset (Set ℝ²)), Q') := by simp
      _ ≤ _ := le_iSup₂_of_le (f := fun I (_ : I ⊆ {Q}) =>
          ⨆ (_ : IsIndependent I), volume (⋃ Q' ∈ I, Q')) {Q} h2 (le_iSup_of_le h1 le_rfl)

/-- The family consisting of the unit square alone has value $1$. In particular `radoValues` is
nonempty, so it has a unique greatest lower bound. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem one_mem_radoValues : 1 ∈ radoValues := by
  refine ⟨{axisParallelSquare 0 1}, fun Q hQ => ⟨0, 1, one_pos, Finset.mem_singleton.mp hQ⟩,
    ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [volume_axisParallelSquare]
  · simp [maxIndependentArea_singleton, volume_axisParallelSquare]

/--
**The covering problem of Rado.**
If the union of finitely many axis-parallel squares has unit area, how small can the largest
area covered by a subfamily of pairwise disjoint squares be? That is, what is the greatest lower
bound $F(\text{square})$ of the largest area covered by an independent subfamily, taken over all
finite families of axis-parallel squares whose union has area $1$?

Here "disjoint" is read as having disjoint interiors, so squares of the subfamily may touch
along their boundaries. This does not change the value of $F(\text{square})$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado : IsGLB radoValues answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
**Radó's conjecture** [Ra28]: every finite family of axis-parallel squares whose union has area
$1$ contains an independent subfamily covering area at least $1/4$, and the constant $1/4$ cannot
be improved, i.e. $F(\text{square}) = 1/4$. This was disproved by Ajtai [Aj73].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.rado_conjecture : ¬ IsGLB radoValues (1 / 4) := by
  sorry

/--
Radó [Ra28] proved that every finite family of axis-parallel squares whose union has area $1$
contains an independent subfamily covering area at least $1/9$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.rado_lower_bound : 1 / 9 ∈ lowerBounds radoValues := by
  sorry

/--
Ajtai [Aj73] disproved Radó's conjecture by constructing a finite family of axis-parallel squares
for which every independent subfamily covers at most $1/4 - 1/1728$ of the area of the union.
Hence $F(\text{square}) \leq 1/4 - 1/1728 = 431/1728$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.ajtai_upper_bound : sInf radoValues ≤ 431 / 1728 := by
  sorry

/--
Bereg, Dumitrescu and Jiang [BDJ10] proved that every finite family of axis-parallel squares whose
union has area $1$ contains an independent subfamily covering area at least $1/8.4797$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.bereg_dumitrescu_jiang_lower_bound :
    1 / 8.4797 ∈ lowerBounds radoValues := by
  sorry

/--
Bereg, Dumitrescu and Jiang [BDJ10] proved that $F(\text{square}) \leq 1/4 - 1/384 = 95/384$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.bereg_dumitrescu_jiang_upper_bound :
    sInf radoValues ≤ 95 / 384 := by
  sorry

/--
Radó's conjecture holds for families of congruent squares (Sokolin, R. Rado, Zalgaller): every
finite family of axis-parallel squares of a common side length whose union has area $1$ contains
an independent subfamily covering area at least $1/4$, and the constant $1/4$ cannot be improved.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem covering_problem_of_rado.variants.congruent_squares :
    IsGLB {maxIndependentArea S | (S : Finset (Set ℝ²))
      (_ : ∃ s : ℝ, 0 < s ∧ ∀ Q ∈ S, ∃ a, Q = axisParallelSquare a s)
      (_ : volume (⋃ Q ∈ S, Q) = 1)} (1 / 4) := by
  sorry

end CoveringProblemOfRado

items: 'Disjoint' subfamily is read as pairwise disjoint *interiors* (touching along boundaries allowed), as suggested by the decomposition notes. This does not change the infimum: shrinking/enlarging every square about its centre by a factor 1∓ε shows the two readings (interior-disjoint vs. closed-set-disjoint) give the same constant, and all lower bounds (≥1/9, ≥1/8.4797) transfer since strictly disjoint implies interior-disjoint.

Squares are closed sets `axisParallelSquare a s = {p | ∀ i, p i ∈ Set.Icc (a i) (a i + s)}` in `ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` with side length `0 < s`; degenerate (side 0) squares are excluded, which is harmless since they have measure zero.
The family is a `Finset (Set ℝ²)` (so repeated squares are identified); this does not affect the constant.

The 'largest area covered by a disjoint subset' is `volume (⋃ Q ∈ I, Q)` (area covered) rather than `∑ volume Q`; these coincide for interior-disjoint squares since boundaries have measure zero. The supremum `⨆ I ⊆ S, IsIndependent I, …` is attained because S has finitely many subfamilies.

'How small can it be' is rendered as the greatest lower bound (`IsGLB … answer(sorry)`) in `ℝ≥0∞`, following MoserWorm.lean; the answer set is nonempty (test `one_mem_radoValues`) so the GLB is unique. The normalisation 'union has unit area' is taken literally as in the statement; by scaling it is equivalent to the inf of ratios |I|/|S| in the Wikipedia article.

Beyond the slot, the file adds related solved results as separate declarations: `rado_conjecture : ¬ IsGLB radoValues (1/4)` (Radó's refuted conjecture F = 1/4, stated negated), `rado_lower_bound : 1/9 ∈ lowerBounds radoValues`, `ajtai_upper_bound : sInf radoValues ≤ 431/1728` (= 1/4 − 1/1728; stated via sInf rather than an explicit witness so it is robust to Ajtai's exact disjointness convention), `bereg_dumitrescu_jiang_lower_bound : 1/8.4797 ∈ lowerBounds radoValues`, `bereg_dumitrescu_jiang_upper_bound : sInf radoValues ≤ 95/384` (= 1/4 − 1/384), and `rado_conjecture_congruent_squares : IsGLB {…same side length…} (1/4)` (sharpness checked by hand via n×n grids of unit squares with corners (i/n, j/n), whose normalised value 1/(2−1/n)² ↓ 1/4).

ENNReal literals: `1 / 8.4797 : ℝ≥0∞` elaborates via `NNRatCast.toOfScientific`, i.e. the cast of the nonnegative rational 8.4797, and truncated ENNReal subtraction is avoided by writing 431/1728 and 95/384 explicitly.
AMS tag 52 (convex and discrete geometry) is used for all statements.

reviewer_notes: Decomposition notes were internally inconsistent: they say the slot Prop should be Radó's refuted 1/4 candidate (research solved, negated) while the header says Status: open and the text_span is the question 'how small can … be?'. Resolved by making the slot the open question `IsGLB radoValues answer(sorry)` (research open, MoserWorm idiom) and including the refuted conjecture as `covering_problem_of_rado.variants.rado_conjecture : ¬ IsGLB radoValues (1 / 4)` (research solved), so both readings are covered. Additional research-solved variants from the Wikipedia article are included in convention-robust forms: Radó's 1/9 lower bound and BDJ's 1/8.4797 lower bound as `∈ lowerBounds radoValues` (valid under the interior-disjoint reading since it only enlarges the set of admissible subfamilies), Ajtai's and BDJ's upper bounds as `sInf radoValues ≤ 431/1728` / `≤ 95/384` (bounds on the infimum, so independent of the exact disjointness convention used in the papers; explicit fractions avoid truncated ENNReal subtraction), and the congruent-squares case as `IsGLB {…} (1/4)` (sharpness checked by hand via n×n grids of unit squares at corners (i/n, j/n)). 'Disjoint' is modelled as pairwise disjoint interiors of closed squares (verified in Lean that the interior is the open square); F is unchanged under the strict-disjointness reading (enlarge each square by 1+ε about its centre), so the modelling choice is immaterial. Normalisation 'union has area 1' is taken literally (equivalent to the |I|/|S| ratio by scaling). One line >100 chars is a URL in the module docstring, as is common in the repo. Compiles with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
